 Judgment

This reference made by the respondent No.1/SLAO, KIADB (Metro Rail Project), Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, 1894 for short), for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. As per the records, the respondent No.1 has acquired the property measuring 96.61 Sq. Meters in Sy.No.1 of Benniganahalli village for the purpose of BMRCL under Preliminary Notification dated 03.02.2018 and Final Notification dated 21.07.2018.
The award passed on 03.01.2019, fixing compensation of Rs.61,65,024/- in this case.
As the dispute is pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.49,32,019/- after deducting 20% Income tax.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Bank of Baroda, Bannerghatta Branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court issued notice to both parties.

In pursuance of the notice, the claimant No.1 Smt. Lakshmi had entered appearance and claimant No.2 Smt. B.N. Tarakumari did not appear before the Court and hence the claimant No.2 has been placed exparte.

.4. The claimant No.1 Lakshmi filed claim statement, wherein she stated about acquisition of property by issuing notifications and depositing of the compensation to the Court in respect of the property bearing No.113, Khatha No.113/1 measuring 96.61 Sq. Meters.

The claim of the claimant No.1 is that she is L.A.C. No. 117/2019 the absolute owner of the property bearing No. 113, khatha No. 113/1, property No.1 situated at Benniganahalli village of Bengaluru East Taluka and the said property has been purchased by her under a registered sale deed dated 20.08.2011 and her property is measuring East to West 40 feet and North to South 26 feet.

It is also claimed by the claimant No.1 that the claimant No.2 in order to make unlawful gain in respect of the compensation awarded to the property of the claimant No.1 filed a suit in O.S. No. 8025/2018 on the file of CCH-30, which is pending before the Court and also claimed that the claimant No.2 preferred a Writ Petition in W.P.No. 50721/2018 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, wherein, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka disposed off the said writ petition, wherein, the order reads as that "The respondent KIADB / SLAO cannot be restrained in disbursing the compensation to the private respondents herein, so long as they fulfill all other requirements.

However, during the course of the L.A.C.117/2019 arguments, the learned counsels representing the private respondents have admitted and undertaken that if the suit filed by the petitioner (petitioner No.1 herein) is allowed Lakshmi vs Slao, Karnataka Industrial Area ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15740001/
2 and if it is found that the lands in Sy. No.1 / Gramatana No.1 as notified by the KIADB belongs to petitioner (First petitioner herein) herein and not the private respondent herein, the private respondents shall refund the compensation to the KIADB / SLAO.".

.5. The respondent No.2 has filed detailed objection statement stating that it has sent the package compensation of Rs.1,44,42,470/- in respect of 96.61 Sq. Meters in the name of Smt. Lakshmi W/o Pallani Swamy through a letter No. BMRCL / LAQ / PH-II / Reach-1E package/5-1/2018-19/567 dated 13.11.2018 L.A.C. No. 117/2019 to enable passing of consent award under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act and also stated that the SLAO passed the General Award dated 03.01.2019 awarding compensation of Rs.61,65,024/- and deposited a sum of Rs. 49,32,019/- in the Court as per cheque No. 035184 dated 20.02.2019 after deducting the tax amount of Rs. 12,33,005/- and accordingly prayed to pass the suitable order.
.6. In order to prove her case, the claimant No.1 Smt. P. Lakshmi is examined as PW.1.

The documents marked at Ex.P.1 to 16.
.7.
On the basis of the above, the points for consideration are that:
1 ) Whether the claimant No.1 proves that she is the absolute owner of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation?
2) What order or award?

Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the affirmative Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .9. Point No.1: The claimant No.1 Smt. Lakshmi claimed that she is the absolute owner of the acquired property and the said property has been purchased by her under a registered sale deed dated 20.08.2011.
Accordingly, claimed that she is entitled for entire compensation in respect of the property involved in this case.
.10. The claimant No.1 in support of her case examined herself as PW.1 by filing evidence affidavit, wherein, she stated in-consonance with the claim statement averments.
The claimant No.1/PW.1 has produced documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 in support of L.A.C. No. 117/2019 her claim over the property involved in this case.
Ex.P.1 is the GPA executed by claimant No.2 Smt. B.N. Tarakumari and her brother B.N. Champak Kumar in favour of one K. Rajeswari in respect of the property involved in this case.

As per the recitals in the said GPA, the claimant No.2 B.N.

sentences.text: On the basis of the aforesaid GPA-Ex.P.1, the said Smt. K. Rajeswari sold the property in favour of this claimant No.1 under a registered sale deed dated 20.08.2011.
The said sale deed has been produced before the Court at Ex.P.2.

The recitals in the said sale deed at Ex.P.2 sufficiently disclose that Smt. K. Rajeswari being a power of attorney holder of claimant No.2 B.N. Tarakumari and her brother B.N. Champak L.A.C.117/2019 Kumar executed a sale deed for valid consideration.

At this juncture, it is also relevant to note that as per recitals in the GPA at Ex.P.1, the claimant No.2 B.N. Tarakumari and her brother B.N. Champak Kumar sold the property to Smt. K. Rajeswari and thereafter, executed the power of attorney.
Therefore, while executing power of attorney in favour of Smt. K. Rajeswari, the claimant No.2 and her brother have received the consideration amount in respect of their property.

.12. On the basis of the aforesaid sale deed at Ex.P.2, the property has been mutated in the name of claimant No.1 Smt. Lakshmi which is evident from the other documents produced by the claimant No.1 in the case.
There is no material on record to show that the said sale deed has been cancelled or modified or declared as null and void.
As such, certainly the said sale deed is binding on other claimants unless and until it has been cancelled or declared as null and void.
Therefore, the materials on record at this juncture sufficiently shows that this claimant No.1 is the absolute owner of the property in involved in this case.
.13. In the case on hand, inspite of service of notice sent to the claimant No.2 through RPAD, the claimant No.2 not chosen to appear before the Court to resist the case.

However, even according to the claim statement of claimant No.1, the claimant No.2 B.N. Tarakumari filed a suit in O.S. No.
8025/2018 for declaration to declare herself as owner of the acquired property which is still pending for disposal.
However, at this juncture, it is also relevant to note the order passed in W.P.No.50721/2018.
But certified copy of the order of the said writ petition is in the file.
The para No. 13 of the judgment is relevant and deciding this case.
"The respondent KIADB / SLAO cannot be restrained in disbursing the compensation to the private respondents herein, so long as they fulfill all other requirements.

However, during the course of the arguments, L.A.C.117/2019 the learned counsels representing the private respondents have admitted and undertaken that if the suit filed by the petitioner (petitioner No.1 herein) is allowed and if it is found that the lands in Sy. No.1 / Gramatana No.1 as notified by the KIADB belongs to petitioner (First petitioner herein) herein and not the private respondent herein,
the private respondents shall refund the compensation to the KIADB / SLAO."

sentences.text: As per the aforesaid observation, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka itself held that the private persons are entitled to receive the compensation, if they satisfy the legal requirements as contemplated under the provisions of the Karnataka Land Acquisition Act.

As discussed earlier, the claimant No.1 claims that she has become an absolute owner of the property on the basis of the sale deed and claimed that on the basis of the said sale deed at Ex.P.2, she acquired valid right, title and interest over the said property.
Till this date, the said sale deed has not been declared as null and void by L.A.C. No. 117/2019 the Competent Court.

Of-course, the claimant No.2 filed a suit in O.S.
No. 8025/2018 to declare herself as owner of the suit schedule property.

However, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No. 50721/2018 specifically held that if at all the private persons or claimants received the compensation amount, they have to give undertaking to the Court before withdrawing the money, that they will refund the compensation to the KIADB / SLAO.
Therefore, by imposing condition as directed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.50721/2018, the claim of the claimant No.1 can be allowed.
Apart from that though the claimant No.2 served with the notice, not chosen to appear before the Court and not put forth any claim in this case.
Accordingly, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
.14. Point No.2:

In view of my finding on the above point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
L.A.C.117/2019 ORDER
The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in respect of claimant No.1 Smt. Lakshmi is hereby allowed.
The Claimant No.1 Smt. Lakshmi is entitled to receive compensation in measuring 96.61 Sq. Meters of Benniganahalli village, along with statutory benefits.

The above claimant No.1 shall has to execute an indemnity bond with one surety,
undertaking to re- deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount she is going to receive in this case.

The claimant No.1 before withdrawing the compensation amount shall give undertaking to the Court that in the event the claimant No.2 succeeds in O.S. No. L.A.C. No. 117/2019 8025/2018, the claimant No.1 will refund the entire compensation amount within a month from the date of judgment / decree in O.S. No.8025/2018.
The reference against claimant No.2 Smt. B.N. Tarakumari is hereby dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
